question:
Peter lives near a rectangular field that is filled with blackberry bushes. The field is \(10\) meters long and \(8\) meters wide, and Peter can reach any blackberries that are within \(1\) meter of an edge of the field. The portion of the field he can reach is shaded in the figure below. What fraction of the area of the field can Peter reach?

[Figure 1](figures/2026_AMC_8_Q06_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The unreachable middle is a rectangle, so subtracting its area avoids counting the corner portions of the border twice.

The whole field has area
\[
10\cdot8=80\text{ square meters}.
\]
The unreachable rectangle begins \(1\) meter inward from each edge. Its length loses \(1\) meter at both ends, and so does its width. Its dimensions are therefore
\[
10-2=8\text{ meters},\qquad 8-2=6\text{ meters}.
\]
Its area is \(8\cdot6=48\) square meters, leaving \(80-48=32\) square meters that Peter can reach. The reachable fraction is
\[
\frac{32}{80}=\boxed{\frac25},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).

edges.reason: The tiled-region interpretation explains what length times width counts. The Geometric Measurement Progression develops that interpretation before treating multiplication as a formula; knowing the formula alone does not certify the tiling procedure.
edges.scope: Understanding rectangle and square area formulas as counts of square units

edges.reason: The rectangle/square area formulas count equal square units, so the meaning of area and its uniform unit are part of the asserted result.
edges.scope: interpreting length times width as unit-square count

edges.reason: The criterion expressly permits rectangle partitions as an alternative to triangle partitions. Retain each route conditionally rather than conjoin the area formulas for every figure. edges.scope: Calculating rectangular pieces in a rectangular partition of a composite area

edges.reason: A general fraction takes several equal unit parts; one such part is the unit-fraction concept directly contained in that construction.
edges.scope: fraction as a count of unit fractional parts

edges.reason: The criteria expressly find common factors and reduce until numerator and denominator are coprime. These are the common-factor contents of the endpoint; finding the greatest factor in a single step is only a shortcut and is outside this required scope.
edges.scope: Finding a shared divisor and recognizing the absence of a shared divisor above one when reducing to simplest form

edges.reason: Reduction replaces numerator and denominator by division by the same common factor, using the value-preserving fraction property.
edges.scope: dividing numerator and denominator by a common number
